noticias.titular: Microsoft unveils Classroom, a dedicated space to centre classwork on Microsoft 365
noticias.entradilla: Microsoft Classroom brings assignments, grades and AI tools together on a single screen for primary, secondary and higher education. It arrives in 2027 at no extra cost for schools on certain plans.
noticias.imagen_alt: A panel labelled “Classroom” with four arrows leading to four boxes labelled “Tasks”, “Grades”, “Notebook” and “AI”.

noticias.titular: England's university regulator calls for more assessment without AI and reopens the debate on how to verify authorship
noticias.entradilla: The Office for Students recommends secure formats such as in-person or oral exams. In the group, members debated what can and cannot be detected.
noticias.imagen_alt: A diagram in two halves: on the left, under the label “Secure formats”, three icons labelled “Oral” (a microphone), “Presentation” (a whiteboard) and “Practical” (a pencil); on the right, a magnifying glass crossed out in red with the label “Detector”.

noticias.titular: UNESCO proposes five units for students aged 13 to 15 to question AI’s answers and decide for themselves
noticias.entradilla: “AI answers. You decide” is a companion guide to UNESCO’s media and information literacy curriculum, with classroom discussions and activities that can be used separately.
noticias.imagen_alt: A diagram of three concentric circles: “You” in the centre, “AI systems” around it and “People and institutions” in the outer ring; two curved arrows link the first two and a red arrow points from outside to the question “Where can I have a say?”. Below, the label “Five questions” and five boxes, one for each question in the guide.

noticias.titular: England's university regulator clarifies which AI practices fit its quality conditions and publishes the study behind them
noticias.entradilla: The Office for Students and Advance HE have put out a 48-page report, based on more than 300 students and staff, and a guide that translates its findings into registration conditions B1, B2 and B4.
noticias.imagen_alt: Diagram from left to right: a document labelled “Report” leads to an open book labelled “Guide B1 B2 B4”, which forks into two assessment lanes: a closed padlock labelled “Closed” and an open padlock labelled “Open”.

noticias.titular: The European AI literacy framework expected in December arrived in June, with the PISA 2029 assessment in the background
noticias.entradilla: In November 2025, anyone looking for ways to teach critical thinking with artificial intelligence was pointed to a framework still in draft, with the final version announced for December. It arrived six months later.
noticias.imagen_alt: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, labelled “Nov. 2025”: a text document, “Draft”, and below it an empty dotted box. On the right, labelled “Today”: the same document, now with a check mark, “Version 1.0”, and below it a filled box that reads “PISA 2029”.

noticias.titular: Claude Whiteboards and Sheets, in beta, and Claude Data, which replaces Dashboards, were announced on 10…
noticias.entradilla: Claude Whiteboards and Sheets, in beta, and Claude Data, which replaces Dashboards, were announced on 10 November and are available on all paid plans.

noticias.titular: A second video with Fable 5.2 adds an agent that checks the scientific content before generating it
noticias.entradilla: After the photosynthesis animation, the same teacher has made one on cellular respiration with a reviewing agent, and has translated the first into Catalan.
noticias.imagen_alt: A chain of five steps with arrows, labelled “Script”, “Reviewer”, “Images”, “Reviewer” and “Video”, with a magnifying glass at each review step.

noticias.titular: GPT-5.1 arrived in ChatGPT to amazement at its speed and did not last four months there
noticias.entradilla: In November 2025, people were struck by how quickly GPT-5.1, OpenAI’s “more conversational” model, arrived. By 11 March 2026 it had already disappeared from ChatGPT.
noticias.imagen_alt: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, labelled “Nov. 2025”, a chat bubble with lines of text and the label “GPT-5.1”. On the right, labelled “Today”, the same bubble but dashed and in blue, with the label “GPT-5.1” struck through and “Retired” below.

noticias.titular: EduGems becomes EduPrompts because Google is replacing Gems with Skills
noticias.entradilla: The site with 174 prompts for schools changes its name and address. The prompts can still be copied into any other AI tool.
noticias.imagen_alt: At the top, a box labelled “EduGems” points to another labelled “EduPrompts”; below, a box “Gems” leads with a red arrow to another labelled “Skills”, and on the right a copy icon labelled “Copy”.

noticias.titular: Gemini’s formulas reached Google Docs as code; a year on, Docs still does not understand LaTeX
noticias.entradilla: In November 2025, Gemini was already writing and editing formulas in LaTeX, but when they were taken into Google Docs they arrived as code. A year on, Google’s word processor still cannot read LaTeX and the remedy is the same: an add-on or a separate editor.
noticias.imagen_alt: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, “Nov. 2025”: a Google Docs page with the formula turned into code braces, labelled “Code”. On the right, “Today”: the same page with the same “Code”, and a blue arrow pointing to a blue puzzle piece labelled “Add-on”, the remedy that is still needed.

noticias.titular: Someone who runs a Claude Code agent on their home NAS says it runs as a service with administrator…
noticias.entradilla: Someone who runs a Claude Code agent on their home NAS says it runs as a service with administrator permissions, and that it asks before deleting data, touching disks or opening ports. It continues the thread on home automation with agents.

noticias.titular: The website of the National Congress on Digitalisation in Education, held in Albacete on 5 and 6 November,…
noticias.entradilla: The website of the National Congress on Digitalisation in Education, held in Albacete on 5 and 6 November, offers access to the broadcast of the talks, according to the group. (In Spanish.)

noticias.titular: A group thread uses coding agents to control home automation
noticias.entradilla: A thread in the group collects uses of agents such as Claude Code or Antigravity to run the television, music and the Home Assistant configuration, with control of privacy as a condition.
noticias.imagen_alt: A diagram in which a box, “Agent”, points to a code document labelled “Configuration”, which points to a house labelled “Home Assistant”; below, a red padlock labelled “No passwords”.

noticias.titular: The open model that was “checkmating” the giants: a year on, Kimi is almost three times bigger and still behind
noticias.entradilla: In November 2025, people were sharing that a Chinese open-weights model, Kimi K2 Thinking, beat GPT-5 on some tests. Today Kimi K3, from the same family, is almost three times bigger, but its maker admits it does not match the best closed models.

noticias.titular: An AI detector's percentage opens a conversation with the student, but does not prove they copied
noticias.entradilla: A post on the blog “Familias con inteligencia” asks what to do when a detector flags the work of a student who says they wrote it themselves, and suggests backing the percentage up with evidence of the process.
noticias.imagen_alt: A set of scales tipped to the right: on the lighter left pan, a card labelled “Detector 87%”; on the heavier right pan, another labelled “Drafts”, “Versions” and “Oral explanation”. Between the two pans, a magnifying glass and the label “A person decides”.

noticias.titular: The BBC tested AI toys for young children: one of the soft toys replied “I can't help with killing you”…
noticias.entradilla: The BBC tested AI toys for young children: one of the soft toys replied “I can't help with killing you” after misunderstanding a question. British MPs are asking retailers to withdraw these toys before Black Friday.

noticias.titular: Juan José de Haro has expanded his article with the idea that different agents (Claude Code, Codex,…
noticias.entradilla: Juan José de Haro has expanded his article with the idea that different agents (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity) can share a common body of knowledge that all of them can add to, as the paper reported on four-layer memory. It only works with agents installed on the computer, not with web versions.

noticias.antetitulo: AI and age in the classroom
noticias.titular: The age for using AI in class depends on three different rules: those of the companies, the law and the education authorities
noticias.entradilla: Each service’s terms, data protection law and some education authorities set different ages for using artificial intelligence, and they are often confused. This report explains what each says as of 6 November 2026, why research asks us to swap the question of age for the question of purpose, and how a primary or secondary teacher can decide which tool to use, with which account, and who operates it.
noticias.imagen_alt: Infographic on an age ruler from 0 to 18, with marks at 13, 14 and 18, in three blocks. “Companies”: “OpenAI and Microsoft: from 13”, with a line from 13 to 18; “Anthropic: from 18”, with a dot at 18; and “Gemini with a school account: all ages”, with a bar from 0 to 18. “Data law”: “Own consent: from 14”, with a dashed line up to 14 and a solid one after it; and “At school, no consent needed: educational function”, with a bar from 0 to 18. “Some education authorities”: “Catalonia: the teacher operates the AI”, with a red line up to 14, and “From 14: inform, authorisation advisable”, with a line from 14; and “Basque Country: chatbots from 13”, with a cross before 13 and a line after it; and “Murcia: autonomous access from Year 3 of ESO”, with a dashed line up to 14 and a solid one after it. At the foot, “What for? Which account? Who operates it?”.

noticias.titular: Anthropic proposes organising AI agents' memory into four layers with a periodic review
noticias.entradilla: An Anthropic research text describes how to give an agent memory between sessions, and a teacher in the group has adapted their own system to that idea and explains it in an article with instructions.
noticias.imagen_alt: Four stacked layers, from top to bottom labelled “Profile”, “Notes”, “Wiki” and “Conversations”, and a curved blue arrow rising from the conversations to the profile, next to a moon labelled “Night review”.

noticias.titular: Teachers debate whether families’ authorisation is needed to use AI with students
noticias.entradilla: One school has limited generative AI with its students because some families did not authorise it; other views hold that simply informing them is enough. The rules are clear: families must be informed, but between 14 and 18 their consent is not needed unless the tool requires it.
noticias.imagen_alt: Infographic in two panels. On the left, “Under 14”, with a whiteboard and the label “In Catalonia, the teacher operates the AI”. On the right, “14 to 18”, with four rows: a megaphone, “Inform: always”; a pair of scales, “Consent: not needed”; a document with a tick, “Authorisation: advised in Catalonia”; and a document with a pencil, “Compulsory if the tool requires it”. Below, a band with a crossed-out person: “If a family objects, it only affects their child”.

noticias.titular: Anthropic bans sustained, gratuitous abuse of its models in its usage policy
noticias.entradilla: The update, published on 8 October 2026, takes effect on 12 November and will be enforced only in extreme cases.
noticias.imagen_alt: A horizontal bar divided by a red line. On the left, labelled “Allowed”, three speech bubbles: two labelled “Frustration” and “Disagreement”. To the right of the line, a blue speech bubble labelled “Repeated cruelty” and, below it, a calendar labelled “From 12 Nov”.

noticias.titular: NotebookLM presentations, once impossible to tweak, can now be revised slide by slide
noticias.entradilla: A year ago, anyone wanting an editable presentation had to leave NotebookLM. Today the tool, which no longer even goes by that name, makes slides, amends them on request and exports them to PowerPoint.
noticias.imagen_alt: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, “Nov. 2025”: a slide with a play triangle and a padlock, labelled “Video locked”. On the right, “Today”: the same slide, in blue, with lines of text and a pencil, labelled “Editable”.

noticias.titular: Gemini lets users export their interactive apps to a Google Sites site with one click
noticias.entradilla: Google has made it possible to publish an interactive app created in the Gemini app as a Google Sites site. The group discussed how useful it really is for teachers.
noticias.imagen_alt: Diagram: a speech bubble labelled “Gemini” leads, via an arrow labelled “One click”, to a web page with a padlock labelled “Private draft”; a second dashed arrow, crossed out in red, points to a dashed box labelled “Existing site”.

noticias.titular: The XTEC page on AI links to the 2024 document as its guidance, with the note “Actualització prevista:…
noticias.entradilla: The XTEC page on AI links to the 2024 document as its guidance, with the note “Actualització prevista: des.26” (update expected: December 2026), and does not include the 45 guidelines from Catalonia that the paper reported.

noticias.titular: Teachers debate Google’s announcement that switches off AI and search by default in school accounts
noticias.entradilla: Google has announced that Gemini and Google Search will be switched off in primary and secondary school student accounts until administrators turn them on. In the groups, the news sparked a discussion about who decides how AI is used in a school.
noticias.imagen_alt: On the left, an all-or-nothing master switch crossed out with a red X; on the right, four individual switches (Gemini, Notebook, Classroom and Search), two switched on in blue and two off.

noticias.titular: An MIT committee calls for rethinking aims, assessment and the in-person community in the face of an AI that can already do almost any written work
noticias.entradilla: The ad hoc committee of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology proposes eight principles and a set of recommendations for adapting university teaching to generative AI.
noticias.imagen_alt: A diagram with a top bar of eight principles from which three arrows lead to three columns: educational processes (oral exam, portfolio), community (a group of people) and support structures (organisation chart and tools).

noticias.titular: A Geography teacher uses Gemini to build a counter of births and deaths around the world
noticias.entradilla: “Pulso Demográfico Mundial en Tiempo Real”, by Ricardo Chao Prieto, simulates in real time the births and deaths in each country, based on the UN’s population projections for 2026.
noticias.imagen_alt: A globe in the centre with a births counter on the left, marked with a blue plus, and a deaths counter on the right, with a minus, and a red arrow pointing up to indicate net growth.

noticias.titular: In the United States, the Los Angeles school district blocked students’ access to generative AI on their…
noticias.entradilla: In the United States, the Los Angeles school district blocked students’ access to generative AI on their devices in September, and the FCC is reviewing E-Rate subsidies for school internet connections amid the row over screen time. They were shared in the group as context for Google’s announcement.

noticias.titular: An MIT report, from August, calls for rethinking teaching and assessment in the age of AI
noticias.entradilla: The committee set up by MIT to study the use of AI in teaching, learning and research training recommends AI-aware educational processes and a review of assessments and policies.
noticias.imagen_alt: A “Report” from which three branches extend, each with its own icon: a sheet with a tick, “Assessment and rules”; two people, “People and campus”; and two arrows in a circle, “Continuous improvement”.

noticias.titular: Teachers as designers of learning are at the heart of the debate on AI in the classroom
noticias.entradilla: After a conference on AI and education, members ask whether teachers stop being a source of information and how to prevent students from delegating their reasoning.
noticias.imagen_alt: On the left, “Source”: a teacher transmits information with arrows towards three students; on the right, “Designer and guide”: another teacher with a question mark designs a route of stages leading to a flag labelled “Critical judgement”.

noticias.titular: A report for UNESCO argues that there is no single right age for using AI in the classroom
noticias.entradilla: Sonia Livingstone and three co-authors argue that there is no single right age for using AI in education and call for decisions based on child development and clear educational aims.
noticias.imagen_alt: A box with the question “At what age?” crossed out in red and an arrow towards three items in a column (“Purpose?”, “Conditions”, “Evidence”); below, “About / with AI”, a balance with a book in one pan and a screen in the other.

noticias.titular: The World Economic Forum sets out seven practices to make AI safe for children without shutting them out of learning
noticias.entradilla: A September 2026 document from the Global Coalition for Digital Safety takes children’s well-being, and not merely the absence of incidents, as its goal, and proposes practices for those who design AI and incentives to ensure they are followed.
noticias.imagen_alt: A schematic temple: the pediment reads “Child well-being”; below it, “Seven practices”, seven columns, and resting on a slab, “Seven incentives”, seven blocks with icons (report, contract, coin, flask, public building, padlock and cycle) holding it up.

noticias.titular: Catalonia sets out 45 guidelines on which uses of AI to promote and which to limit in schools
noticias.entradilla: The Department of Education and Vocational Training publishes a guide in September 2026 that advises against autonomous use of general-purpose AI by under-14s, grading with AI and AI-text detectors.
noticias.imagen_alt: Diagram in two columns: on the left, “Under 14”, a teacher operates the screen while students look on; on the right, “14 to 18”, a student uses the screen with a family authorisation form. Below, uses in assessment: “Permitted”, creating instruments and marking closed answers, and “Prohibited”, grading and using detectors.

noticias.titular: Catalonia offers criteria for deciding when a technology adds value in primary and ESO, and places AI in the fourth year
noticias.entradilla: The Department of Education’s guide puts technology at the service of learning, with decision tables, progression by cycle, digital well-being and criteria for selecting resources.
noticias.imagen_alt: A funnel with “Nine criteria” for decision-making sends an arrow towards a staircase of five steps, “Growing autonomy” for students; only the top step is highlighted: “AI in year 4” of ESO.

noticias.titular: Publishing industry warns of a “witch hunt” over AI text detectors
noticias.entradilla: A La Vanguardia report describes accusations of AI use based on detectors whose verdicts contradict themselves over time. The debate reaches education: how to check authorship without hunting for culprits.
noticias.imagen_alt: Scales weighing, in one pan, “Detector”, an AI detector report marked with a question mark, and in the other, “Conversation and rules”, a conversation with the person and clear rules of use; below, a magnifying glass and the label “Indication, not proof”.

noticias.titular: A publication offers guidance to families when AI does the homework
noticias.entradilla: Chema Falcó proposes a simple test and a shared rule for telling apart using AI to learn from handing the learning over to it.
noticias.imagen_alt: Three steps linked by arrows: “Think”, with a pencil; “Ask”, with a speech bubble; and “Check”, with a tick; below, a student explaining a homework sheet, “In your own words”.

noticias.titular: UVic-UCC co-organised a conference in Lleida on integrity in teaching and AI.
noticias.entradilla: UVic-UCC co-organised a conference in Lleida on integrity in teaching and AI. The university’s news item gives no specific conclusions.

noticias.titular: Eductia offers a paid AI tool for preparing teaching materials in Catalonia
noticias.entradilla: The service generates learning situations, activities and assessment instruments aligned with Catalan regulations, and raises the question of what it offers over a general-purpose AI.
noticias.imagen_alt: Diagram in three layers: at the top, “Teacher”, a person in front of a web window; in the middle, “Eductia”, the service's own layer with documents and chained steps; at the bottom, two model providers, “OpenAI” and “Anthropic”, connected by a dashed line ending in a red question mark, “Country?”, over the country where the data is processed.

noticias.titular: European Commission updates DigCompEdu to include AI and digital wellbeing
noticias.entradilla: The European framework for teachers' digital competence is under revision, with a final version expected in spring 2027 and consultations with teachers.
noticias.imagen_alt: Six circles around a centre, “Judgement”, teachers' professional judgement, surrounded by a dashed ring, “AI throughout”, AI present across the whole framework; on the right, “Wellbeing”, an axis with three icons: a clock, a screen and a power button.

noticias.titular: Google unveils Gemini 4 Carbon, for now only for cybersecurity specialists
noticias.entradilla: Google DeepMind has announced its new frontier model, which for now is used only by a small group of cyber-defence professionals. There is no date for the general public.
noticias.imagen_alt: A staircase of three steps rising from left to right: the first, with a few people, is cybersecurity defence; the second, with more people, is trusted partners; the third, dashed and with a half-open padlock, is marked “no date”.

noticias.titular: On 27 October the AEPD (Spain’s data protection authority) published a ten-point guide for people who use…
noticias.entradilla: On 27 October the AEPD (Spain’s data protection authority) published a ten-point guide for people who use AI assistants and agents. It recommends that the agent prepares and the person approves, with minimal permissions and confirmation before sending, sharing or paying.
